In preparation to depict human agony in this painting, the artist repeatedly visited the Hospital Beaujon to sketch dying patients. As he began his final version of this work, he reversed the orientation of an early attempt titled "Sighting of the Argus," making the main action and figures face right. Only the legs and torso of the figure in the lower right can be seen, while four huddled figures create a structural triangle with the vessel's mast in the central left. Depicting the survivors of a shipwreck near Mauritania, FTP name this 1819 work by Theodore Gericault.

Outdoor night-time shots in this film were lit by red magnesium flares, and another of its innovations was the use of the iris effect for close-ups. An early scene depicts a housekeeper named Lydia attempting to flirt with Charles Sumner, while his dismissal of her leads her to spit after him and tear her shirt in frustrated desire. Late in the film Flora Cameron jumps to her death rather than submit to the lustful advance of the Black Union soldier Gus, leading her brother Ben to bring the Ku Klux Klan to the rescue of Southerners suffering under Reconstruction. So runs the ugly plot of, FTP, what film described as "history written with lightning" by Woodrow Wilson, the first epic silent film directed by D.W. Griffith?

His etchings include series of illustrations for an edition of Gogol's Dead Souls, the Bible, and the Fables of La Fontaine, and he designed sets and costumes for 1945 and 1970 stagings of Stravinsky's The Firebird. The Art Institute of Chicago is home to this man's painting The White Crucifixion and his America Windows. He also created a set of twelve stained glass windows for the synagogue of Hebrew University's Hadassah Medical Center but is more well known for his gouache paintings, including Cow with Parasol and The Green Violinist.FTP name this Russian-Jewish artist of I and the Village.

A work by this composer was adapted into the finale of Brahms' Symhpony No. 4, and the magnum opus of Heitor Villa-Lobos is a nine piece collection named for this man. Wendy Carlos popularized the Moog synthesizer in the album titled Switched-On this composer. One work of his was based on a theme by Frederick the Great, and another contains 30 variations on an aria. In addition to The Musical Offering and the Goldberg Variations, he composed a cantata that contains the movement "Jesu, Joy of Man's Desiring."The prefix BWV identifies this German's compositions, which include The Well-Tempered Clavier. Name this Baroque composer of the Brandenburg Concertos.

The title cup dominates a cloudy landscape in this painter's The Giant's Chalice and a mountain pass is depicted in his The Notch in the White Mountains. One series of paintings by this artist includes works like The Savage State, Consummation, and Decline, while another comprises Childhood, Youth, Manhood, and Old Age. Due to his many depictions of its landscapes, the fourth tallest of the Catskills mountains is named for him. Founder of Hudson River School, FTP, name this painter of the two series of paintings The Voyage of Life and The Course of Empire

One work by this artist features a halo-encircled Apollo talking to the title blacksmith. In addition to The Forge of Vulcan, this artist depicted Justinus of Nassau handing the keys to the titular Dutch city to General Ambrogio di Spinola in The Surrender of Breda. One work by this artist features Roman goddess of love lying on her bed and looking at herself in a mirror held by Cupid. This artist of The Toilet of Venus created a notable portrait of Pope Innocent X and was the court painter of King Philip IV. The most famous work by this artist features a large dog, dwarfs, and maids, all of whom surround the Infanta Margarita. Name this Spanish painter of Las Meninas.

This composer's fifth symphony was inspired by Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress, while his fourth, in F minor, shows the influence of Jean Sibelius. His seventh symphony is derived from music he'd been writing for a film about the explorer Robert Scott and is known as the Sinfonia Antarctica. Better known is his first symphony, incorporating text from Walt Whitman and titled A Sea Symphony and his third, A London Symphony. FTP name this 20th-century British composer who also wrote fantasias on Thomas Tallis and "Greensleeves."

"Bear Dance" is the final movement of his Ten Easy Pieces for piano, and "Six Dances in Bulgarian Rhythm" concludes his collection of 153 piano pieces entitled Mikrokosmos. "First Seduction Game" is a section of his pantomime ballet The Miraculous Mandarin, and "The Lake of Tears" is a piece from this composer's only opera, in which the new bride Judith is given seven keys. This composer of Duke Bluebeard's Castle collected folk songs with fellow countryman Zoltan Kodaly. FTP name this composer of Music for Strings, Percussion and Celesta and Concerto for Orchestra, a Hungarian.

The painting "Battle of Lights, Coney Island" is an indicative work of this art movement, created by American Joseph Stella, another of whose works fitting this movement is a five-panel altarpiece depicting bridges and buildings called "New York, Interpreted." A crescent moon is overwhelmed by the light from the title object in another work of this movement, "Street Light," while a sculpture of a rippling figure striding forward purposely also depicts this movement's emphasis on dynamism. Including works like "Unique Forms of Continuity in Space," FTP name this early 20th-century movement created by Italians like Umberto Boccioni and Giacomo Balla.

One opera by this composer ends with Death departing and Satyavan coming back to life. In addition to Savitri, he composed the opera At the Boar's Head. Orchestral works by this composer include the Thomas Hardy inspired tone poem Egdon Heath, and a work named for the school where he taught, St. Paul's Suite. The movements "Song of the Blacksmith" and "Fantasia on the Dargason" conclude his Second Suite in F for Military Band. His best-known work was inspired by astrology and contains seven movements, the first of which features an ostinato rhythm in 5/4, and is entitled "Mars, the Bringer of War." name this English composer of The Planets.

Gérard Presgurvic wrote a musical about this story "de la Haine à l'Amour" in 2001, and Vaccai and Bellini wrote rival operas based on Italian sources for this story. Hector Berlioz wrote a symphony about it that finds the title character alone at a party in the second movement and uses the its description of dreamers for the "Queen Mab Scherzo." Charles Gounod wrote an opera based on this play, while Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky composed a "Fantasy Overture" about it. Identify this play that more famously inspired a ballet by Sergei Prokofiev and the Leonard Bernstein's musical West Side Story.

The opening sequence of Robert Bresson's cult classic Mouchette features a trapped one. In the film adaptation of Stephen King's Riding the Bullet, one is devoured by a rabid dog that is promptly run over by a car. Michael Moore documents a woman who raises them for income, slaughtering them at the age of four months in Roger and Me. In Fatal Attraction, Glenn Close boils one belonging to her lover's daughter. Name this type of creature that guards the Cave of Caerbannog in Monty Python and the Holy Grail and tells Donnie Darko that the world will end 28 days, 6 hours, 42 minutes, and 12 seconds.

This artist's innovative String Quintet in C Major alternates between minor and major tones as evidenced by the sudden shift of the G tone in the second movement. This musician didn't meet with much success from such operas as The Devil's Palace of Desire or The Friends of Salamanca. This composer's adroitness at setting such texts as "Der Doppelganger" and "Gretchen at the Spinning Wheel" gained him fame for developing the lieder. Name this Austrian composer most famous for symphonies including his "The Great" and "Unfinished."

This artist adapted The Last Tycoon and The French Lieutenant's Woman to his preferred medium in 1976 and 1981, respectively. This writer's works for radio include A Slight Ache, but his reputation was made by The Caretaker. One of his works finds Meg planning a certain event for Stanley while, in another, Ben is ordered to kill Gus in directions received via a titular device. Name this author of The Birthday Party and The Dumbwaiter; a British playwright who won the 2005 Literature Nobel.

Uncharacteristic works by this artist include the semi-Gothic Episcopal Palace of Astroga, while his artist's early works like the Vicens House and Güell Estate are in the so-called Moorish style. Later embracing the fervor of the Renaixensa, this designer created the Casa Batlló and Casa Milá. Most of this architect's work, including the still-unfinished Sagrada Familia, is located in and around Barcelona. Name this Catalan architect of the early twentieth century notable for his voluptuous, organic forms.

Lesser-known early members of this group include Johannes Itten and László Moholy-Nagy, who founded a so-called New version of it. Teaching using the interplay between a Form Master and craftsman, this school inspired "Point and Line to Plane" by its most famous instructor and employed Georg Muche, Marcel Breuer, Lyonel Feininger, Paul Klee, and Wassily Kandinsky. Hannes Meyer took over for its most famous head, Walter Gropius. Name this seminal German school of architecture and design whose name means "home of building."

This artist's early Scherzo for violin & piano in C minor displays the dual influences of Reményi and Joachim and is the third part of the "F A E" Sonata. This composer's work took a turn for the lighter with his Liebeslieder of 1868, composed approximately contemporaneously with his Hungarian Dances. His St. Anthony Variations are on a theme of Haydn, and the Tragic Overture showcases his Romanticism. Name this German composer of the Academic Festival Overture and, a German known for his four symphonies.

Luigi Cherubini's work of this type uses demisemiquavers to depict the "deep lake," while Hector Berlioz's was written on commission from Gasparin and ineptly conducted by Habeneck. Antonín Dvořák's is ninety five minutes long and Britten wrote a version known as War. Verdi's is particularly noted for its Agnus Dei. Franz Süssmayr completed a famous work in this genre that was left unfinished by its composer's death. Name this type composition of which Mozart's is perhaps the best-known; a musical setting of the Mass for the Dead.

The base of this work contains a rusted chain next to a wound scroll. A man in white sits with bowed head at the left while another white-haired man clutches his head at the right. Three figures ascend a staircase in the background, behind a man who despairingly presses his forehead into a stone wall. To the right of the title figure are six men, one of whom grabs the title figure's left leg; that title figure points skyward, reaching with his left hand for the chalice that will cause the title event. Identify this painting by Jacques-Louis David, about a philosopher's execution.

This artist's work The Prodigal Son reflects his Cubist period, while a so-called totemic period is represented by the wood pieces Adam and Eve and King of Kings, designed for his planned Temple of Meditation. Margit Pogany modeled for the marble abstracted from a woman craning her neck to look in a mirror, Princess X, while Renèe Frachon is depicted in the Muse and Sleeping Muse series. Name this sculptor of the limestone The Kiss and the metallic series of Birds in Space who walked to Paris from Romania to begin his art career.

Composing "Fallen sick on a journey" from his deathbed, this artist utilized the penname Sobo for one notable collaborative work. His school collaborated on The Monkey's Straw Raincoat and the name by which he is known comes from a favorite hut near a plantain tree. Many of this writer's works display a love for the old known as sabi; this is often especially evident in his travelogues Records of a Travel-Worn Satchel and The Narrow Road to the Deep North. Name this Edo-period Japanese poet; the best-known writer of haiku.

He underwent hypnosis therapy before returning to composition, and won a gold medal for his one-act opera Aleko. An Edgar Allan Poe poem provided the inspiration for his tone poem The Bells, while it was an Arnold Bocklin painting resulted in his work The Isle of the Dead. Inspired by a work of 24 Caprices by a certain violinist, he composed what may be his best-known work. Name this Russian composer of Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini.

In an opera by this composer, the titular wizard hides his death in the tears of his daughter, and in another, the title character wagers that he can catch golden fish in Lake Ilmen. In addition to Kashchey the Immortal and Sadko, this man is known for orchestral works like the Russian Easter Festival Overture. Also known is his "Scene and Gypsy Song," the fourth movement of Capriccio Espagnole, and "The Sea and Sinbad's Ship," the first movement of Scheherazade. Name this Russian who created the opera The Tale of Tsar Saltan, which features the interlude "Flight of the Bumblebee."

This person wrote two contradances for Count Czernin as well as a mock- heroic funeral march for "Signor Maestro Contrapunto." He composed variations on "La belle Francoise" and "Ah! Vous dirae-je maman," as well as the Odense and Paris symphonies, while his early works, like the Sonata in C major, were composed in Salzburg. All of his works are categorized by Köchel numbers, while his better-known pieces include the "Ave verum corpus" and Jupiter symphony. Name this German composer of Eine Kleine Nachtmusik and the opera The Magic Flute.

This artist convinced Segei Shchukin to let him alter the color scheme of one of his works before it was purchased. His Seated Riffian shows the title character in a green shadow, while Green Stripe shows his wife in a Japanese hairstyle. Many of his works from the early twentieth century feature a motif of five nude forms holding hands and dancing in a circle. Name this French Post-Impressionist, creator of The Red Room, The Joy of Life, and the series La Danse and The Blue Nude.

The sonata with this name opens with a loud C minor chord, and the opening of the first movement is marked grave [grah-VAY]. The second movement, an Adagio cantabile, is in rondo form. A symphony with the same byname begins with a theme in E minor played by the bassoons and has a waltz-like second movement except for its 5/4 time signature. The sonata was arguably its composer's most important early work, while the symphony was its composer's last, as he died shortly after its 1893 completion. Give the shared name of Beethoven's Piano Sonata No. 8 and Tchaikovsky's Symphony No. 6, named for their melancholic emotiveness.

This work and its predecessor, Woman with Plants, represent a stylistic turning point for their artist. This picture's Art Institute exhibition won its artist a 300-dollar prize. Many who felt they were represented by a woman in this painting wrote the artist directly to complain. The other figure in the painting was modeled by Dr. Byron McKeeby, the artist's dentist, who stands in front of the titular type of roof, which caps a house that still stands in Eldon, Iowa. Identify this instantly recognizable painting of a farmer and his daughter by Grant Wood.

The Boston Public Library is home to his Frieze of Prophets, a work from his mural cycle Triumph of Religion. Taught by Carolus-Duran, he was appointed War Artist during World War I and evoked the horrors of war in Gassed. He was called "the Van Dyck of our times" after completing Lady Agnew of Lochnaw. Two towering vases appear in The Daughters of Edward Darley Boit. Two girls light up Chinese lanterns in Carnation, Lily, Lily, Rose, and his most famous work depicts Pierre Gautreau's pale wife in a black dress. Name this artist of Madame X.

This artist commemorated children killed in a church bombing in "Alabama." His band's bassists were Steve Davis, Reggie Workman, and Jimmy Garrison. He toured with altoist Eddie "Cleanhead" Vinson after working at a sugar refinery and serving the Navy in Hawaii. He teams with only percussionist Rashied Ali on Interstellar Space. He worked with Miles Davis on ‘Round Midnight and Kind of Blue and underwent a spiritual change after recording "My Favorite Things." name this tenor saxophonist who recorded Giant Steps and, with Elvin Jones and McCoy Tyner, A Love Supreme; the pioneer of free jazz.

Located next to Parnassus and Disputa, this work's left side finds one bald man copying over the shoulder of another On the right, men holding a sphere and a globe each look down at the work in progress. Located at the Stanza della Segnatura, this painting shows the aforementioned Averroes on the left and Zoroaster, Ptolemy, and Euclid, a portrait of Bramante, on the right. Epicurus reads in the left corner and a portrait of Michaelangelo writes in the center. Aristotle points his palm to earth while Da Vinci look-alike Plato points upward. Name this Vatican fresco by Raphael.

This man's later works include an Entry of the Crusaders into Constantinople and two depictions of lion hunts. This artist painted a group of murals for the Salon du Roi at the Palais-Bourbon. A Byronic poem inspired his The Death of Sardanapalus, while his tour of North Africa resulted in The Women of Algiers. He depicted a tragedy of the Greek war of independence in The Massacre at Chios but he's better known for depicting himself in a tophat alongside a woman with bared breasts and a boy with pistols. Identify this French artist who created Liberty Leading the People.

This person depicted the upper class in such works as Racing at Longchamp and View of the International Exhibition and lesser-known works by this man include a painting of his sister-in-law Berthe Morisot and a portrait of his friend, Émile Zola. His better-known works include Music in the Tuileries and a work that has a trapeze artist performing above the title restaurant's customers. Painter of A Bar at the Folies-Bergère, this is, which French painter bridging the gap between Realism and Impressionism and perhaps best known for Olympia and Luncheon on the Grass?

His fourth symphony, often nicknamed "Ode to Heavenly Joy", uses a Wunderhorn song for soprano, while his third is unnamed. His ninth and tenth symphonies are unfinished, while his second uses a certain Klopstock ode. His first symphony in D major is known as the "Titan", while his sixth is known as the "Tragic". Name this Austrian composer whose eighth symphony requires eight soloists, a double choir, and orchestra, and is thus known as the "Symphony of a Thousand".

The death of this man's lover, Mamah Cheney, inspired the second of two works near Spring Green, Wisconsin, while one of his most famous creations was for Edgar Kaufmann, Sr. His other works include the Charnley Building, the Larkin Building in Buffalo and the Robie House on the south side of Chicago. Highly associated with Oak Park, Illinois, name this American architect of Taliesin and Fallingwater, whom Apu claims is the designer of Marge Simpson's hair.

All of the icons in this film are derived from the church where the director's father delivered sermons. In it, Plog's wife seduces one of the players in a nearby town while a seminary student speaks condescendingly to Mia's husband, Jof, which results in Squire Jons' cutting him with a knife. Drawing its title from Chapter 8 of Revelation, it takes place as the Black Death ravages the countryside and shows a knight playing chess with Death in order to postpone his own demise. Name this classic 1957 film starring Max von Sydow, perhaps the most famous of director Ingmar Bergman.

Paco Bugallo has worked on a large pictorial illustration of pieces of this painting and some argue that the artist's alienation with it mirrors that involving his son, George-Hippolyte. In the foreground, a man covered in red stares off into space. A figure in the background waves a shirt. The dark colors on the far left and right punctuate the tone of the scene, which is somber despite the strong sail on the left, because of all the dead people on- board. Name this 1819 painting depicting the survivors of a famous shipwreck, a work of Theodore Gericault.

This composer tested the limits of the sonata form in his Opus 16 Piano Concerto and Opus 27 String quartet in G minor. His Lyric Pieces are not to be missed and his Opus 40 "from the time of" a previous composer is known as the "Holberg Suite." However, his greatest fame rests in a piece with such movements as "The Death of Ase," "Anitra's Dance" and "In the Hall of the Mountain King." name this composer best known for his incidental music for Peer Gynt and for being Norwegian.

He collaborated on the libretto of William Grant Still's Troubled Island, an opera about political turmoil in Haiti. He also worked on the play Mule Bone, though worked independently on his biography of Marian Anderson and his autobiographical The Big Sea. He portrays Sandy's acknowledgement of the realities of life in a small town in his novel Not Without Laughter, but is better known for his poetry collections including Fields of Wonder and Shakespeare in Harlem. Name this poet of "The Weary Blues" and "The Negro Speaks of Rivers"

He replaced Matthew Locke as the composer for royal string orchestra and was appointed organist of Westminster Abbey in 1679, replacing the composer John Blow. His death of an unknown illness prevented him from completing the operatic version of John Dryden's The Indian Queen. This wasn't his only collaboration with that poet, as he also wrote music to Dryden's Tytannick Love, and Amphitryon. He often adapted Shakespeare, as in his operatic version of A Midsummer Night's Dream entitled The Fairy-Queen. For ten points name this Baroque English composer of Dido and Aeneas.

Much of this man's best work, including his later Sonata in B Minor and a Barcarolle were composed during summers spent at Nohant. A student of Joseph Elsner, one of this man's early compositions was arranged for the military band of the Russian Grand Duke Constantine, and after coming to Paris under the auspices of Baron Rothschild, he composed a Ballade in G Minor and the Fantasie-Impomptu. Better known compositions by this man include two piano concertos and numerous polonaises. Identify this composer best known for his "Grand Etudes," including a "Revolutionary" one, and various waltzes and mazurkas.

A student of Simone Peterzano, this man completed the Seven Acts of Mercy for the Pio Monte della Misericordia, and as payment for admission into the Order of St. John, he painted a Beheading of St. John in which he signed his name in the blood. Some of this man's most famous paintings were commissioned for the Contarelli Chapel, while his early secular works include The Card- Sharps and The Fortune Teller, as well as a painting of himself as a Sick Bacchus. Famous for his innovative use of chiaroscuro and tenebrism, identify this Baroque painter of The Calling of St. Matthew, The Conversion of St. Paul, and Supper at Emmaus.

One of this architect's early focuses was developing homes commissioned individually, such as those of Raoul La Roche and Michael Stein. He published a work that applied mathematical proportions in the human body to architecture to create a scale of proportions that defined his late architecture, Le Modulor. His workers' community, Pessac, was shunned because it did not respect the local architecture of Bordeaux, but nonetheless he was selected in 1951 to develop the Indian city of Chandigarh. Name this French architect and proponent of the international style, who promoted his five points of modern architecture in his Villa Savoye.

After the death of Sita, Shiva created the demon Vīrabhadra by performing this action on himself. The city of Megara fell to King Minos after Scylla performed this action on King Nisus. According to the Skáldskaparmál, the sons of Ivaldi crafted Skidbladnir and Mjollnir after Loki atoned for performing this action as a prank on the wife of Thor, Sif. The Book of Judges describes how a Nazarite was blinded and imprisoned in Gaza after a servant performed this action on him. Name this action which caused the loss of strength of Samson.

Benjamin Britten based his Young Persons's Guide to the Orchestra on the theme of this man's Abdelazar. This man's mentor composed the masque Venus and Adonis and was named John Blow. His compositions were collected by his widow in Orpheus Britannicus, whose preface was written by a son of this man's contemporary and friend John Playford. He composed operas based on King Arthur and Spenser's The Faerie Queen, and another of his operas contained the noted aria "When I am Laid in Earth." name this English Baroque composer of Dido and Aeneas.

An alligator and three turban-clan men on horseback attack the titular black African mammal in this artist's painting The Hippopotamus Hunt. This artist portrayed Triton blowing a seashell beneath Cybele and Neptune in his painting The Union of Earth and Water, and his more violent paintings include Allegory of Peace and War and the recently discovered Massacre of the Innocents. His wife Hélène Fourment modeled for his paintings The Three Graces and The Garden of Love. He also painted a cycle of canvases about Marie de Medici, as well as a painting of men trying to raise the body of Christ, The Elevation of the Cross. Name this Baroque Flemish painter known for his fleshy nudes.

Canova created a nude sculpture of this figure holding an apple and a spear posing as Mars the Peacemaker. His portrait where he is holding a staff with a pointing hand on the end of it is often compared to God the Father from the Ghent Altarpiece, a portrait by Ingres. Antoine-Jean Gros depicted touching soldiers dying of the plague at the Pesthouse in Jaffa. He is shown crowing his kneeling wife in a coronation portrait by the artist of The Sabine Women. Identify this man shown on his horse crossing the Alps by David.

Notable creations of this civilization include the Kunz Axe which shows a figure crossing its arms and a child holding a were-jaguar in the Las Limas Monument. Some scholars have hypothesized that their most famous relics also doubled as thrones, and their writing system is demonstrated on the Cascajal Block at their site at San Lorenzo. They constructed a Great Pyramid at La Venta, and they are named for the Nahuatl word for "rubber people", as they probably originated the ballgame. Identify this ancient civilization of Mesoamerica, best known for their colossal stone heads.

This man composed a Romance for the unusual instrumentation of a harmonica and full orchestra. This man wrote a set of five songs that incorporate George Herbert poems, Five Mystical Songs, and his choral works include To An Unknown Region and The Sacred City. More well-known works by this composer include three Norfolk Rhapsodies. Other works by this composer include operas based on Pilgrim's Progress and Synge's Riders to the Sea. Identify this composer of Fantasia on a Theme of Thomas Tallis and Simphonia Antarctica.

The Galleria Borghese contains two self-portraits by this man done seven years apart, as a "Young Man" and "Mature Man." He designed a large bronze, four-legged structure known as the "baldachino" for St. Peter's Basilica, and along with his father Pietro, he completed the Fontana della Barcaccia that contains a sculpted ship; that fountain is located below the Spanish Steps. This sculptor of Angel with the Crown of Thorns and The Rape of Proserpina also sculpted a work that is flanked by balconies of statues of Florentine nobles, who look on a scene topped with gilded rays in which an angel pierces the title figure with an arrow. Name this sculptor of The Ecstasy of St. Theresa.

One character in this work sings the aria "Parmi veder la lagrime" after learning about the abduction of a character whom he met earlier when disguised as Gualtier Maldè. That character is the subject of the aria "Caro Nome" and at the beginning of this work he sings "Quaesta o Quella" when he attempts to seduce Countess Ceprano. Based on Victor Hugo's play Le Roi s'amuse, the title character is cursed by Monterone for aiding the Duke of Mantua in his flings and unwittingly aids in the abduction of his daughter Gilda, who is killed by the assassin Sparafucile. Featuring the aria "La donna è mobile," identify this Giuseppe Verdi opera about a hunchbacked court jester.

King Midas is shown with donkey ears in this artist's painting Calumny, and he painted the panel entitled Fortitude in a seven part series illustrating the seven great virtues. His early biblical scenes include The Return of Judith to Bethulia and The Discovery of the Body of Holofernes, and his works The Trials of Moses, The Trials of Jesus, and The Punishment of the Rebels are in the Sistine Chapel. In one of his more famous painting, a partially naked male god is resting, but is provoked by some satyrs as the other female deity watches the scene, and he inserted Chloris, Flora, and Zephyrus in one of his most famous works. Name this Florentine artist best known for Mars and Venus, Primavera and The Birth of Venus.

The minuet from Bizet's The Fair Maid of Perth features solos by a harp, a flute, and one of these, while Vaughan Williams' Symphony No. 6 notably features one of these among the woodwinds. Other solos for them can be found in the "Old Castle" section of Mussorgsky's Pictures at an Exhibition and Percy Grainger's Lincolnshire Posy. An orchestration of Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue includes five different varieties of this instrument. Ravel's Bolero uses their sopranino variety, while other varieties include the B-flat tenor and the E-flat baritone and alto. FTP, name this family of transposing instruments, famously played by Charlie Parker and John Coltrane.

This man's operas The Devil's Palace of Desire and Fernando were flops. He composed the lied "Die Forelle," which became the basis for his popular Trout Quintet. He wrote incidental music to the play Rosamunde in addition to the Little C Major symphony. Like Mahler, he did a Tragic symphony, and this composer's lieder include "Der Erlkonig," "Death and the Maiden," and "Gretchen at the Spinning Wheel." name this composer whose work was catalogued by Otto Deutsch, the composer of the Unfinished Eighth symphony.

Strings and a bassoon arpeggio open this composer's Op. 53a, which ends abruptly and violently, presumably with the death of one title figure, Pan and Echo. Surusoitto, or Funeral Music, composed in 1931 is thought to be one of the few links to his destroyed Eighth Symphony, which was to follow his Seventh in C Major, which uniquely has a single movement and was originally called a "fantasia sinfonica". One of his most famous pieces is the third movement of a suite of Four Legends of Lemminkäinen, while another was written as a rousing call for his nation's independence. Name this composer, best known for the tone and symphonic poems The Swan of Tuonela and Finlandia.

The bare head of a young person, possibly a child, droops the back and right in this artist's bust Suffering, while this artist's The Prayer presents a dark woman, with a featureless face, leaning far forward. He executed several versions of La Négresse Blonde, and many of his works feature carefully carved, wooden bases, which he felt was important to their presentation. The Gate of the Kiss was constructed as a memorial to soldiers of World War I along with the more famous Table of Silence and Infinite Column. More famous works include a head laying on its side, Sleeping Muse, and the series The Kiss. FTP, name this Romanian artist best known for his series of sculptures Bird in Space.

This architect designed his house in Lincoln, Massachusetts, and eight buildings enclose a series of quadrangles in his design for the Harvard Graduate Center. One of this architect's designs features one section with a white facade with a red-brick top. That section juts above the rest, which is mostly in yellow brick, as does a tall yellow brick tower in a building designed as a shoemaking factory. This architect had even the corner stairwells visible to the public in his Administration Building for the Werkbund Exhibition in Cologne. Besides the Fagus Works, his best-known work has a pinwheel layout with three wings connected by a bridge across a street. Much like lots of this man's work, that building features a steel or concrete framework with a lot of glass, and is located in Dessau. FTP, name this designer and founder of the Bauhaus.

The background of one of this man's portraits shows an owl being attacked by birds, as well as a man standing on a Gothic tower, praying to a star painted with real gold. In another work, a cavalier stands before a tent at the right, while wrinkled old women are carted over to a large pool. His works are often signed with the winged serpent of his insignia, while Cupid ensconced in a black cloud aims at a nude Venus in one of this man's depictions of The Judgment of Paris.
